title: Double Chocolate Focaccia
changes_from_base: Sweet cocoa dough with chopped dark chocolate, baked in a smaller tin and finished with pearl sugar.
summary: A sweet, bubbly cocoa focaccia laced with melting dark chocolate and topped with crunchy sugar.
equipment: cling film or a clean tea towel

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa, salt, yeast, warm water, 1 tbsp oil and vanilla until no dry patches remain, cover and rest 20 min.

steps.title: Develop
steps.text: Beat with a paddle on medium speed 10-12 min, or give the dough six sets of bowl folds 20 min apart, until it stretches in long strands. Mix in the chopped chocolate briefly. A well-developed dough traps the gas and stays bubbly despite the cocoa.

steps.title: Rise
steps.text: Cover and leave in a warm place about 1 h, until slightly puffy.

steps.title: Tin
steps.text: Oil the tin with 2 tbsp oil, scrape in the dough and press it to the edges with oiled fingers. Cover and leave 2-3 h, until very puffy with bubbles on the surface.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Drizzle with the last 1 tbsp oil, dimple gently and sprinkle with the pearl or demerara sugar.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 25-28 min; the dark colour hides browning, so go by the probe, which should read about 96 °C, and a firm, crisp base. Cool 20 min in the tin before cutting into 9.

tips: Use a probe to check doneness; the dark crumb hides any browning.
A common mistake is under-mixing; the dough must stretch in strands before the chocolate goes in.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep wrapped at room temperature for up to 2 days; warm at 180 °C for 4-5 min. Freeze for up to 1 month.
